enriched_description: Small shorebird measuring 17-21 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 37-42 cm. Breeding plumage displays rich chestnut-red back and wing coverts contrasting with dark brown crown and black belly patch. Non-breeding plumage is uniform grey-brown above with white underparts. Bill is medium-length, slightly decurved, and dark. Legs are dark grey to black and relatively short. Wings are pointed with white wing stripe visible in flight. Tail is short and slightly forked. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with compact streamlined profile. White eyebrow stripe contrasts with dark eye line. Weight ranges 40-70 grams. Distinctive hunched feeding posture with rapid pecking motion.

Medium-sized wading bird measuring 24-27 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 53-58 cm. Plumage is mottled brown above with heavily streaked breast and white belly. Most distinctive feature is bright red-orange legs, long and slender, visible even at distance. Bill is moderately long, straight, and slightly upturned at base, red at base transitioning to dark tip. Wings display white trailing edge and white rump visible in flight. Tail is short with white edges. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with medium-length neck. Eye is dark with pale orbital ring. Weight ranges 80-140 grams. Alarm call is loud ringing 'teu-hu' giving species its name.

Medium-sized shorebird measuring 24-32 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 45-52 cm. Plumage varies by season: breeding adults display rich rufous-orange underparts with barred flanks and olive-green back with black centers; non-breeding plumage is uniform grey-brown above with pale grey underparts. Bill is very long, straight, and dark, measuring 5-7 cm, specialized for probing mud. Legs are yellowish-green to olive and moderately long. Wings are pointed with white rump and tail edges visible in flight. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with stocky profile. Supercilium (eyebrow stripe) is pale contrasting with dark crown. Weight ranges 70-130 grams. Feeding behavior features rapid side-to-side bill sweeping motion.

Medium-large shorebird measuring 40-50 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 72-85 cm. Plumage is striking black and white: entirely black head, neck, and upperparts contrasting with pure white underparts and wing bars. Most distinctive feature is long, laterally compressed, bright orange-red bill with chisel-like tip adapted for prying open mollusk shells. Legs are pinkish-red and stout. Eyes are yellow with prominent red orbital ring. Wings are broad with bold white wing bars visible in flight. Tail is black with white base. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with robust stocky build. Weight ranges 400-800 grams. Loud piping call carries along coastlines.

Very large waterbird measuring 130-180 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 200-300 cm depending on species. Plumage is predominantly white, grey, or brown depending on species and season. Most distinctive feature is enormous bill with distensible gular pouch extending from lower mandible, used for scooping fish. Bill measures 30-45 cm with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding. Neck is long and S-curved. Legs are short and webbed with all four toes connected. Wings are extremely broad and long with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body. Tail is short and wedge-shaped. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with heavy barrel-shaped torso. Weight ranges 4-15 kg. Soaring flight with neck retracted.

Large penguin measuring 85-95 cm in height with distinctive black and white plumage. Head, back, and flippers are glossy black with vibrant orange-yellow auricular patches extending from ear region down neck sides. Breast and belly are white transitioning to pale yellow on upper breast. Bill is long, slender, and black with bright orange-pink lower mandible and base. Flippers are stiff and paddle-shaped, black on both surfaces. Feet are black and webbed. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with upright torpedo-shaped profile adapted for swimming. Neck is elongated with orange coloration. Juveniles display brown-grey plumage lacking orange markings. Weight ranges 9-18 kg. Flightless; swims using flipper propulsion.

Very large seabird measuring 80-135 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 200-350 cm, the largest of any living bird. Plumage is predominantly white with dark brown to black upperwings, back, and tail depending on species. Head and underparts are white. Bill is massive, long, and hooked at tip, composed of multiple horny plates, yellow to pink with dark tip. Nostrils (nares) are tubular and positioned on sides of bill. Legs are pink to flesh-colored with webbed feet. Wings are extremely long and narrow, optimized for dynamic soaring. Tail is wedge-shaped. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with streamlined profile. Weight ranges 3-12 kg. Capable of hours of flight without flapping.

Medium-sized baleen whale measuring 12-15 meters in length with robust spindle-shaped body. Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches created by barnacles and whale lice (cyamids). Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top. No dorsal fin present; instead displays 6-12 dorsal knuckles (humps) along posterior back. Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, measuring 2-3 meters. Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch. Baleen plates are cream-colored, numbering 130-180 per side, used for filter-feeding. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 15-35 tons. Skin texture is rough with callosities.

Large toothed whale measuring 6-9 meters in length with distinctive black and white coloration pattern. Body is predominantly glossy black with contrasting white patches: oval white eye patch behind and slightly above eye, white ventral surface from jaw to tail, and greyish-white saddle patch behind dorsal fin. Dorsal fin is extremely tall and triangular, reaching 1.8 meters in males, shorter and falcate in females. Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, black on outer surface, white on inner. Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge. Head is rounded without distinct beak. Teeth are conical and interlocking, numbering 40-56. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 3-6 tons.

Large aquatic sirenian mammal measuring 2.4-3 meters in length with robust fusiform body. Skin is smooth and hairless, displaying grey to brownish-grey coloration with lighter ventral surface. Head is rounded with broad downturned snout covered in coarse bristles (vibrissae) used for detecting seagrass. Eyes are small and positioned laterally. No external ears visible. Forelimbs modified into broad paddle-shaped flippers without nails. Tail fluke is distinctive bilobate (dolphin-like) shape, horizontal orientation, distinguishing from manatees' rounded paddle tail. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with no dorsal fin. Skin texture is smooth and thick. Weight ranges 230-500 kg. Small downward-curving tusks present in mature males.
